# `sim/particles/ParticleAudioBridge.js`

> **Source:** `engine/sim/particles/ParticleAudioBridge.js`

ParticleAudioBridge.js - Real-Time Procedural Spatial Audio for Particle Systems Zero-latency audio driven by GPU particle events via onParticleEvent callbacks. Every collision triggers sound immediately — no polling, no timers. Architecture informed by FMOD, PopcornFX, and Web Audio API perf research: - HRTF panning — binaural left/right ear simulation with elevation + front/back cues - Spatial clustering — nearby same-material impacts merge into single louder sound - Priority classes — critical/high/normal/low tiers (FMOD-style, not just volume) - Fade-out on voice steal — 5ms gain ramp prevents audible clicks - Separate ambient bus — continuous loops bypass transient compressor (no pumping) - Listener orientation — correct panning from camera forward/up vectors - Shared AudioContext — accepts external context to avoid browser resource limits - Per-material spatial cooldown — dedupes only within a radius, not globally - Dynamic compressor on impact bus — tames peak transients without affecting ambients Usage: const bridge = createAudioBridge({ maxVoices: 32, maxDistance: 100 }); wireEventCallbacks(bridge, world.eventSystem, getMaterialForEvent); // Per-frame (for ambient loops + listener tracking): updateListenerFromCamera(bridge, camera); updateEmitterAmbients(bridge, emitters); // Cleanup: destroyAudioBridge(bridge);

### `createAudioBridge(config = {})`

Create an audio bridge with full voice management.

**Parameters:**

- `config` *(Object)* — _No description in source JSDoc._
- `config.maxVoices` *(number)* — Max concurrent one-shot voices (default 32)
- `config.maxDistance` *(number)* — Max audible distance (default 100)
- `config.masterVolume` *(number)* — Master volume (default 0.5)
- `config.audioContext` *(AudioContext)* — External AudioContext to share (optional)

### `updateListenerFromCamera(bridge, camera)`

Update listener from a camera object. Sets both position AND orientation for correct spatial panning (research: without orientation, all panning is wrong).

### `triggerImpact(bridge, material, position, speed = 2, temperature = 300, priorityClass = PRIORITY_NORMAL, velocity = null)`

Trigger an impact sound immediately. Used for reaction events and manual triggers. For collision/death events, use the batched system (flushImpactBatches) instead.

**Parameters:**

- `priorityClass` *(number)* — PRIORITY_NORMAL by default. Use PRIORITY_HIGH for player-caused.

### `wireEventCallbacks(bridge, eventSystem, getMaterial)`

Wire the bridge into the ParticleEventSystem via onParticleEvent callbacks. Fires immediately when readbackEvents completes — zero polling, zero timers. Registers for collision events (type 2, 3) and death events (type 1).

**Parameters:**

- `bridge` *(Object)* — _No description in source JSDoc._
- `eventSystem` *(Object)* — From initParticleEventSystem
- `getMaterial` *(Function)* — (evt) => substanceKey or materialIndex.

### `unwireEventCallbacks(bridge)`

Unwire event callbacks (for cleanup). Actually removes the callback functions from the event system's callback arrays.

### `resumeAudioContext(bridge)`

Resume AudioContext after browser autoplay policy suspension. Research (Chrome/Safari): Context starts 'suspended' until user gesture. Call this from your first click/keydown handler.

### `autoUnlockAudioContext(bridge)`

Auto-unlock AudioContext on first user interaction (Safari/iOS workaround). Research (Matt Montag): Safari requires resume() from touch/click handler. Registers one-shot listeners that self-remove after first successful resume.

### `pauseAllAudio(bridge)`

Pause all audio (suspend context). Use when tab hidden or game paused. Research (web.dev Fieldrunners): every game should pause audio on tab hide to prevent wasted CPU and audio buildup.

### `resumeAllAudio(bridge)`

Resume all audio after pause.

### `hookVisibilityAutoPause(bridge)`

Hook into Page Visibility API to auto-pause/resume audio. Call once after createAudioBridge.

### `setOcclusionCallback(bridge, fn)`

Set an occlusion callback. The function receives (sourcePos, listenerPos) and returns 0-1 (0=fully occluded, 1=clear). Used to modulate LPF cutoff for obstruction. Game code provides the raycast logic; audio system just applies the result.

### `soloMaterial(bridge, patchKey)`

Debug: solo a specific material (only that material plays). Pass null to clear.

### `muteMaterial(bridge, patchKey)`

Debug: mute a specific material. Pass null to unmute all.

Reset per-frame stats counters for delta profiling. Call after getAudioBridgeStats each frame.

## Notes & Examples

### Physics Engine Integration

The physics system provides rigid body dynamics, collision detection, and raycasting. Bodies have shapes (box, sphere, mesh), mass properties, and constraints. The GPU physics engine accelerates broad-phase collision detection and particle systems.

**Example: Creating physics bodies**
```js
import { PhysicsWorld } from 'engine/physics/PhysicsWorld.js';
import { RigidBody } from 'engine/physics/RigidBody.js';
import { BoxShape, SphereShape } from 'engine/physics/Shapes.js';

const world = new PhysicsWorld({ gravity: [0, -9.8, 0] });

// Static ground
const ground = new RigidBody({
  type: 'static',
  shape: new BoxShape(10, 1, 10),
  position: [0, -0.5, 0]
});
world.addBody(ground);

// Dynamic box
const box = new RigidBody({
  type: 'dynamic',
  mass: 1,
  shape: new BoxShape(1, 1, 1),
  position: [0, 5, 0],
  restitution: 0.5  // Bounciness
});
world.addBody(box);
```

**Advanced: Collision detection and raycasting**
```js
// Raycast to find what the player is looking at
const hit = world.raycast(camera.position, camera.forward, 100);
if (hit) {
  console.log('Hit entity:', hit.body.entityId);
  console.log('Hit point:', hit.point);
  console.log('Hit normal:', hit.normal);
  
  // Apply impulse at hit point
  hit.body.applyImpulse([0, 10, 0], hit.point);
}

// Shapecast (swept sphere) for character movement
const sweep = world.shapecast(
  player.position,           // Start
  desiredPosition,           // End
  new SphereShape(0.5),    // Player capsule radius
  { ignore: player.body }  // Don't collide with self
);
if (sweep.hit) {
  // Slide along wall
  player.position = sweep.position;
}
```

**Advanced: Constraints and joints**
```js
import { HingeConstraint, FixedConstraint } from 'engine/physics/Constraints.js';

// Door hinge
const doorHinge = new HingeConstraint({
  bodyA: doorFrame,
  bodyB: door,
  pivot: [0, 1, 0],      // Hinge location
  axis: [0, 1, 0],       // Hinge axis (Y up)
  limits: [-90, 90]      // Open angle range in degrees
});
world.addConstraint(doorHinge);

// Ragdoll joint (ball-and-socket)
const shoulder = new FixedConstraint({
  bodyA: torso,
  bodyB: arm,
  pivotA: [0.5, 1.5, 0],  // Shoulder position on torso
  pivotB: [0, 0, 0]       // Shoulder position on arm
});
world.addConstraint(shoulder);
```

**Advanced: Continuous collision detection (CCD)**
```js
// Fast-moving objects need CCD to not tunnel through walls
const projectile = new RigidBody({
  type: 'dynamic',
  shape: new SphereShape(0.1),
  mass: 0.1,
  ccd: { enabled: true, sweptSphereRadius: 0.1 },
  linearDamping: 0  // No air resistance for bullets
});
projectile.velocity = [0, 0, 100];  // Very fast
world.addBody(projectile);
```

**Gotchas:**
- **Units**: Physics uses meters, kilograms, seconds. A 1-unit cube is 1 meter.
- **Time step**: Fixed time step (1/60) gives stable simulation; variable dt causes explosions.
- **Collision layers**: Use collision masks to filter what collides (player vs enemy, bullet vs world).
- **Sleeping**: At-rest bodies sleep to save CPU — wake them before applying forces.
